body:
## What

Right-clicking a session in the Agents window sessions list now shows an **Open Pull Request** action when that session is associated with a GitHub pull request. Activating it opens the PR on GitHub (same behavior as the existing session-header PR pill).

## Why

The session header already surfaces a pull request pill, but there was no way to open a session's PR directly from the sessions list without first navigating into the session. This adds the affordance where users right-click.

The action opens the PR externally (browser). It reuses the existing `OpenPullRequestAction`, so both entry points (session-header pill and the new context-menu item) stay in sync.

title: sessions: single source of truth for single-pane layout enablement
body:
## What

Establishes a **single source of truth** for whether the Agents window uses the single-pane (docked detail panel) layout. Previously the experimental setting `sessions.layout.singlePaneDetailPanel` (`DOCK_DETAIL_PANEL_SETTING`) was read directly in many places — both as `config.…` context-key expressions in `when` clauses and as imperative `configurationService.getValue(...)`/`shouldUseSinglePaneLayout(...)` calls at several construction sites.

## Changes

- **Setting is read exactly once** — in `createSessionsWorkbench`, which picks the `Workbench` vs `SinglePaneWorkbench` variant. The redundant `shouldUseSinglePaneLayout` helper was inlined here and removed, so the setting + viewport-width check is no longer re-evaluated at multiple part-construction sites.
- The chosen variant is published two ways:
  - `IAgentWorkbenchLayoutService.isSinglePaneLayoutEnabled` — read by **imperative** code.
  - New `SinglePaneLayoutEnabledContext` context key (set once by the workbench) — read **only** by declarative `when` clauses.
- **Declarative consumers** (`layoutActions`, `editor`/`codeReview`/`changes` contributions, responsive sidebar) now gate on the context key instead of `config.${DOCK_DETAIL_PANEL_SETTING}`.
- **Imperative consumers** (`editorParts`, `paneCompositePartService`, `sessionChangesService`, `sessionChangesEditor`, layout contribution) now read `isSinglePaneLayoutEnabled` off the layout service — never the context key or the setting directly.

## Notes for reviewers

- Context keys are read **only** in `when` clauses; imperative code uses the layout service. This addressed review feedback.
- Minimal environments (component fixtures / tests) register a plain workbench layout service whose `isSinglePaneLayoutEnabled` is falsy, which correctly maps to the classic layout.
- Verified with `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, ESLint, and the pre-commit hygiene hook. Test harness updated to inject a mock layout service.

title: sessions: bridge extension editor/title actions into single-pane editor menu
body:
## What

In the Agents window **single-pane** layout, the editor group renders its title actions from the sessions-owned menu `Menus.SessionsEditorTitle` (via `getGroupViewOptions` in `singlePaneEditorPart.ts`) instead of the core `MenuId.EditorTitle`. This shadowing meant `editor/title` actions contributed by **extensions** disappeared in the single-pane layout.

This PR adds `EditorTitleMenuBridgeContribution` (in the common `contrib/editor/browser/editor.contribution.ts`) that bridges those actions:

- Active only when `isSinglePaneLayoutEnabled`.
- Listens to `MenuRegistry.onDidChangeMenu(MenuId.EditorTitle)` and mirrors items into `Menus.SessionsEditorTitle`.
- Mirrors **only extension-contributed** items, identified by `item.command.source` (set exclusively by the `commands` extension point). Core items have no `source` and are already dual-contributed where needed, so they are not duplicated.
- Keeps the mirror in sync (a `DisposableStore` cleared/rebuilt on each menu change) as extensions register/unregister.

## Why

Extensions contribute editor toolbar actions to `editor/title` → `MenuId.EditorTitle`. The single-pane override replaced that menu, silently removing all such extension actions from the editor title toolbar.

## Notes for reviewers

- Only the `editorActions`/`MenuId.EditorTitle` override hid extension actions. The per-tab context menu uses `MenuId.EditorTitleContext` (hardcoded, not remapped), so extension `editor/title/context` items already work. `Menus.SessionsEditorTabsBarContext` only shadows `MenuId.EditorTabsBarContext`, which has no extension contribution point — nothing lost there.
- Added unit tests (`editorTitleMenuBridge.test.ts`) covering: only extension items bridged, dynamic register/unregister sync, and no-op when single-pane is disabled.

title: sessions: default single-pane side pane to 60% and persist its width reliably
body:
## What

Improves how the single-pane **side pane** (the docked editor part) is sized and persisted in the Agents window.

- **First open → 60%**: revealing the side pane from closed now sizes it to **60% of the window width** (`INITIAL_EDITOR_WIDTH_RATIO`) instead of a 50% main-area split, so the editor content is readable beside the detail.
- **Workbench-level width**: the side-pane width is global (`workbench.sessions.partSizes`), so switching sessions keeps the same width. Hiding the pane in one session no longer resets another session's width on return.
- **Double-click sash → 60%**: double-clicking the chat↔side-pane sash resets the side pane to 60%, via a `preferredWidth` on `SinglePaneMainEditorPart` (single-pane only; the classic layout keeps the standard distribute-on-reset).

## Bug fixes (why the width wasn't sticking)

- **Save aborted on the docked aux bar**: in single-pane the docked auxiliary bar is *not* a grid view, so reading its size threw `View not found` and aborted the whole `_savePartSizes` — the editor width was never persisted. Reworked into a single overridable `_persistedGridViewSize` used for all parts; single-pane returns the docked aux-bar width from the docked layout state instead of the grid. Removed the separate `_persistedAuxiliaryBarWidth` hook.
- **Corrupt `0` width → 300 on reload**: a stale/sub-minimum persisted editor width (e.g. a `0` left by a transient squeeze) was passed through `?? 600` (which doesn't catch `0`), building a 0-width node that the grid clamped to its 300px minimum. Restore now treats sub-minimum as missing → default; save no longer persists a collapsed width while the editor is visible.
- **Editor-only compounding shrink**: `_persistedEditorWidth` subtracts the docked detail width **only when the detail is visible** (mirroring the grid descriptor), so an Editor-only session no longer shrinks by the detail width on every reload.
- **Cross-session reset**: closing the whole side pane in one session used to discard the remembered editor width, so returning to a session reset it to the default. Now the width is captured before the node collapses and restored on reveal.

## Notes for reviewers

- Behavior is **single-pane only**; the classic sessions layout is unchanged (no `preferredWidth` override; `_persistedGridViewSize`/`_persistedEditorWidth` base behavior preserved).
- Reload is flicker-free: the workbench restores the editor node width from its own persisted part-sizes in the grid descriptor, so there's no post-paint resize.
- Docs updated (`LAYOUT.md`, `SINGLE_PANE_SCENARIOS.md`) and a pitfall added to the sessions skill (side-pane size is workbench-level, not per session).
- 54 `Sessions - Workbench` unit tests pass, including new regression tests for each fix; typecheck + layer check clean.

title: sessions: remember Changes editor view state across scenarios
body:
## What

Persist and restore the Agents-window **Changes** editor's multi-diff view state so it survives across scenarios:

- Reloading the window
- Switching sessions (the Changes tab is closed/disposed on switch)
- Toggling the side pane
- Reopening the Changes editor / opening a file diff and returning

State remembered per session: overall scroll position, per-file **collapsed/expanded** state, selections, and **which file was active**.

## Why

The single-pane `SessionChangesEditor` extended plain `EditorPane` and never persisted any view state, whereas the standard workbench `MultiDiffEditor` already does via `AbstractEditorWithViewState`. So collapsing files / scrolling was lost on every navigation.

## Changes

- **`SessionChangesEditor`** now extends `AbstractEditorWithViewState<IMultiDiffEditorViewState>`, keyed by the per-session `multiDiffSource` resource, with `tracksDisposedEditorViewState() === true` so state survives the tab being disposed on a session switch. It also persists on hide (`setEditorVisible(false)`), and defers focus via `onDidChangeActiveControl` so focus lands in the active diff editor even when the editor part was just revealed from a hidden/0-size state.
- **Active-file persistence**: `IMultiDiffEditorViewState` gains `activeDiffItemKey`. Restoring the active item on load makes the widget's existing `if (activeDiffItem) return` guard suppress the automatic first-change navigation (which otherwise expands the first file and resets scroll) — so the restored state wins, without any extra suppression flag.
- **Ordering fix (also fixes standard `MultiDiffEditor`)**: `MultiDiffEditorWidget.setViewModel` now optionally takes the `viewState` and applies the model + view state in a **single transaction**. Previously `setViewModel` set the model outside any transaction, firing the widget's first-change init autorun *before* `setViewState` restored the active item — so for already-loaded diffs it navigated to and focused the **first** file. Both editors now load the view state before `setViewModel` and pass it in.
- Small reusable `saveCurrentEditorViewState()` hook added to `AbstractEditorWithViewState` for the save-on-hide case.

## Notes for reviewers

- The active-item restore is gated on `preserveFocus`: session switches (background) don't steal focus; explicit opens (Changes tab, diff-stats pill) focus the active file's diff.
- There's no editor-pane/widget view-state test harness, so this isn't unit-testable in isolation — it needs a running editor. Manual check: collapse/scroll a non-first file in session A's Changes, switch to B and back (async load), and reopen from a closed side pane (cached load) — collapsed state, scroll, active file and focus should all be preserved.

Fix Modern UI editor tab decoration color on full label
body:
Fixes #325246

## Summary

With Modern UI (`workbench.experimental.modernUI`) enabled, file decoration colors (e.g. git modified / problem colors) no longer tint the editor tab **filename**. Badges still show the decoration color, but the label text is forced to the normal foreground.

Root cause: Modern UI style overrides in `tabs.css` set:

```css
.tab.active .tab-label a { color: var(--vscode-foreground) !important; }
.tab:not(.active) .tab-label a { color: color-mix(...) !important; }
```

Those rules override the decoration color class applied to `.monaco-icon-label` (`monaco-decoration-itemColor-*`), so only badge `::after` colors remain visible.

## Changes

- Exclude labels that carry a `monaco-decoration-itemColor-*` class from the forced Modern UI tab label colors.
- Explicitly inherit the decoration color onto the label name, description, and highlighted label so the **entire** tab label is tinted, matching classic UI.

## How to Test

1. Enable `"workbench.experimental.modernUI": true`.
2. Ensure `"workbench.editor.decorations.colors": true` (default).
3. Open a git-modified file (and/or a file with problems) so the tab has decoration badges.
4. Compare the active/inactive tab label text color with Modern UI off.

Before: filename stays normal foreground; only badges are decoration-colored.
After: the full tab label text uses the decoration color, same as classic UI.

title: Fix inline suggestion false negatives via canonical cursor-edit rebasing
body:
## Why

`toInlineSuggestion` decides whether a next-edit suggestion (NES) renders as ghost text at the cursor (an inline suggestion) or as a NES box (an inline edit). It had frequent false negatives: edits that *could* be shown as ghost text were misclassified as inline edits, so ghost text was suppressed. The motivating real-world case was replacing the next `) {` line with new parameters plus the same `) {` re-appended, which is really an insertion at the cursor but was not detected as one.

## Approach

Instead of a growing pile of prefix/suffix trimming special cases, re-express any edit as the single equivalent edit spanning `cursor -> end-of-line` and validate that one canonical form (`tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`). This form is maximal: if any equivalent inline suggestion exists, one exists here. That subsumes the previous special cases and closes the false-negative family in one place.

`tryAdjustNextLineInsertion` is kept as the fallback used when advanced detection is disabled, but its pull-up is now provably exact: it only accepts when `newText` ends with the document's own line break, then drops that break and re-prepends it at the cursor.

## Notable fixes and trade-offs

- **Spurious blank line**: inserting a block that does not end in `\n` onto an empty next line used to be accepted and produced an extra blank line. It is now correctly rejected (rendered as an inline edit instead).
- **CRLF soundness bug** (latent before this PR): inserting a bare `\n` into a CRLF document produced `a\r\n\r\nb` instead of the true `a\r\n\nb`. Requiring the document's actual line break (not merely `\n`) fixes it. This was surfaced by the strengthened test harness below.
- The rebase is gated behind the existing advanced-detection setting; when it is off, the exact next-line fallback still applies.

## Tests

Added an independent representability oracle plus an exhaustive soundness + completeness harness over both LF and CRLF corpora (every document/cursor/range/newText combination). The harness asserts both that every representable edit is offered and that any offered suggestion reproduces the edit exactly. The soundness direction is what caught the CRLF bug. Also added a named CRLF regression test. Full suite passes (51 tests) and the extension type-checks cleanly.

Inline suggestions could be misclassified as inline edits when a provider expressed a ghost-text-compatible change using a range away from or spanning the cursor line. The existing shape-specific normalization missed valid equivalent ranges.

This change rebases candidate edits to the canonical range from the cursor to the end of its line, while verifying unchanged prefix/suffix text and the existing ghost-text constraints. It preserves exact same-line results and the established next-line insertion fallback.

The tests include the reported next-line replacement regression and an independent finite exhaustive oracle over LF and CRLF documents to verify that every representable edit is detected and remains equivalent.

title: sessions: remember agent mode/approvals picks as new-session defaults
body:
## What

New agent-host (Copilot CLI) sessions now default to the **agent mode** and **approvals** the user last selected in the new-session pickers.

## Why

The pickers already persisted the user's selection to profile storage (`setSessionConfigValue` -> `sessions.agentHost.sessionConfigPicker.selectedValues`), and `_initialNewSessionConfig` read it back — but it then overlaid `chat.defaultConfiguration` read via `getValue()`. That setting ships with a schema default (`{ mode: 'interactive', approvals: 'default' }`), so `getValue()` always returned a value even when the user never configured it, silently overriding the remembered picks on every new session. The setting's own description promises "each session remembers what was used", which was not happening.

## How

`_initialNewSessionConfig` now reads `chat.defaultConfiguration` via `inspect()` instead of `getValue()`, and resolves each axis (`mode`, `approvals`) with the precedence:

**enterprise policy > remembered pick > effective configured value** (`inspect().value` — the user's setting, or the schema default when unset).

- An enterprise **policy** value stays authoritative (wins over the remembered pick).
- An ordinary **configured setting** is treated as a plain default that the remembered pick overrides.
- With nothing configured and nothing remembered, the schema default applies as before.

The independent `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` policy restriction still clamps auto-approve to `default`.

## Tests

Added/updated unit tests in `localAgentHostSessionsProvider.test.ts` covering: remembered picks winning over an ordinary configured setting (with the schema default simulated as in production), a configured setting used when nothing is remembered, and an enterprise policy value overriding remembered picks.

## Notes for reviewers

Change is contained to `src/vs/sessions/`. `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, hygiene, and the `createNewSession` unit tests all pass.

title: MCP: preserve authorization server context on auth re-validation
body:
Fixes #324925

## Problem

When `AuthenticationService` fires `onDidChangeSessions` for a provider, `MainThreadMcp._onDidChangeAuthSessions` re-validates every tracked MCP server using that provider — regardless of *why* the event fired (e.g. an unrelated account being added or removed). That re-validation was calling `_getSessionForProvider` with `authorizationServer` (and `resource`/`clientId`/`audience`/`clientSecret`) dropped to `undefined`, instead of the values the server's session was originally created with.

For the Microsoft provider the tenant is derived from `authorizationServer`; losing it makes the silent token request fall back to the `organizations` authority. Depending on the account/tenant relationship this either silently targets the wrong authority (masking the bug) or, for a single-tenant app with a B2B guest, fails with `AADSTS650059` and the server is torn down with _"Authentication session for {0} removed, stopping server"_.

## Fix

Capture the auth context (`authorizationServer`, `clientId`, `resource`, `audience`, and the secret-storage **key** — not the secret value) in `McpServerAuthTracker` when a server's session is established, and replay it on re-validation. The client secret is re-read from storage by key so a secret rotated via the _Set Client Secret_ code lens takes effect immediately instead of replaying a stale value.

The context is held opaquely by the tracker as a single `IMcpServerAuthContext`, so `MainThreadMcp` stays provider-agnostic — each provider consumes the subset it understands (Entra: authorizationServer/clientId/resource; dynamic DCR: + clientSecret; enterprise/XAA: + audience).

## Testing

**Unit** — new `McpServerAuthTracker` tests (context round-trip, replacement on re-track, untrack, clear).

**E2E A/B** against a real Entra-protected MCP server (tenant-specific authority, resource `api://…/mcp.tools`), triggering re-validation via an unrelated account sign-out:

| | re-validation authority | `resource` |
|---|---|---|
| **Before (unpatched)** | `…/organizations` (5/5) ❌ | dropped ❌ |
| **After (patched)** | `…/<tenant-guid>` (14/14) ✅ | preserved ✅ |

Same server, same trigger, same account — only the patch differs.

## Not yet verified

The hard-teardown path (Evidence 2 in the issue: single-tenant app + B2B guest → `AADSTS650059` → server stopped) is **not** verified end-to-end — the A/B account is a native tenant member, which hits the benign-masking path (`organizations` still resolves). The authority-preservation fix is proven; teardown prevention is inferred from it. Draft partly for this reason.

title: Stop session/customizationsChanged log spam in agent host
body:
## Problem

The agent host was emitting **thousands** of `session/customizationsChanged` envelopes — bursts of ~100+/second during active Claude turns. In a captured log, a single session accumulated ~1,084 of these (7,317 total across 10 sessions).

Two compounding causes:

1. **`ClaudeCustomizationWatcher` triggered on SDK runtime churn.** It recursively watches `~/.claude` and treated *any* change under it as a customization change. But the Claude SDK constantly rewrites runtime data there — `history.jsonl`, `projects/` transcripts (appended on every message/tool call), `tasks/`, `file-history/`, `shell-snapshots/`, `sessions/`, `backups/`, caches — none of which are customization sources.

2. **`_publishSessionCustomizations` dispatched unconditionally.** A single edit under the shared `~/.claude` tree fans out to every open session, and the agent-level `onDidCustomizationsChange` republishes once per session, so one change emitted **O(N²)** identical envelopes.

## Fix

1. **Narrow the watcher trigger scope** (`claudeSessionCustomizationDiscovery.ts`). The recursive watch on `.claude` is unchanged (keeps OS watcher count low), but the change *triggers* are now an allowlist of the actual customization sources — `agents`, `skills`, `commands`, `rules`, `plugins`, `CLAUDE.md`, `settings.json`, `settings.local.json` — plus the existing `.mcp.json` and memory-file triggers.

2. **Add a per-session dedup guard** (`agentSideEffects.ts`). `_publishSessionCustomizations` now skips the dispatch when the resolved customizations are unchanged since the last publish for that session (mirroring the existing `_publishAgentInfos` dedup). The dedup cache is pruned against the live session set on each publish cycle (covers both `deleteSession` and eviction, neither of which emits a signal we subscribe to).

## Verification

Covered by new unit tests **and** verified live in the Agents window against real Claude sessions:

| Scenario | `customizationsChanged` | Before |
|---|---|---|
| One full Claude turn | **1** (correct initial publish) | ~1,084/session |
| 20 rounds runtime churn under `~/.claude` (1 session) | **0** | ~20 × N |
| 30 rounds runtime churn, **3 active sessions** | **0** | hundreds (N² fanout) |
| Add / rename / delete a real customization | **fires** ✅ | — |
| Identical re-touch | **deduped** ✅ | — |

Body-only edits to a rule/agent don't re-emit, which is correct: the event payload carries only the descriptor (`id`/`uri`/`name`/`description`/`model`/`enabled`), never file content, and the workbench consumer uses it solely to refresh the agent picker + customizations tree.

## Notes

- Separate, pre-existing issue not addressed here: repeated `snapshotResolvedCustomizations failed — Subprocess initialization did not complete within 60000ms` warnings (Claude SDK subprocess/auth timeout).

title: Propagate MCP App metadata eagerly for Copilot tool calls
body:
## Why

For MCP-App tools running through the Copilot agent host, the MCP App surface previously only mounted **on tool completion**. That was a workaround: the Copilot SDK didn't surface MCP App `_meta.ui.resourceUri` on `tool.execution_start`, so the host recovered it at `tool.execution_complete`.

The recent SDK version fixes this and surfaces the metadata at tool start. Combined with the invariant that **a tool call cannot begin until its MCP server is `Ready`**, the AHP `mcp://` channel is also available at start — so we can publish the complete `_meta.ui` payload (resourceUri **+** channel) once, at `ChatToolCallStart`, and mount the App eagerly for a running tool.

## What

**Host — `copilotAgentSession.ts`**
- Build `_meta.ui = { resourceUri, channel }` at `tool.execution_start` (the SDK now provides `resourceUri`; the channel is available because the server is already `Ready`).
- Simplify the completion path to just re-emit the tracked meta (the reducer preserves `_meta` when an action passes `undefined`, via `meta ?? tc._meta`).
- Remove `_refreshActiveMcpToolCallUiMeta` and the running-state meta re-emission that only existed to handle "server becomes `Ready` after the tool started" — impossible under the readiness invariant.

**UI — `stateToProgressAdapter.ts`**
- Mount MCP App `toolSpecificData` eagerly for running tool calls in `toolCallStateToInvocation`, rather than only at completion.
- Confirmation-gated tools (created without `mcpAppData`) mount the App on the `PendingConfirmation → Running` transition; the channel is present in `_meta.ui` throughout. This branch leans on `getMcpAppData`'s MCP-contributor check so non-MCP tools fall through to their own handling.

## Tests
- Host: `tool_start` carries MCP App UI metadata; the channel is included in the start meta when the server is already `Ready`.
- UI: MCP App `toolSpecificData` is set for running MCP tool calls; the App mounts when a confirmed MCP tool starts running.

title: Prompt for MCP server auth once per conversation
body:
### Problem

The "The MCP server … requires authentication" prompt shown for agent host sessions reappeared on **every** chat message. The auth-required state is derived from session-wide customization state, but the prompt is emitted from the per-turn observable graph in `_observeTurn`, so each turn independently re-surfaced it.

### Fix

Track, per session, which MCP servers have already had an auth prompt surfaced in the current conversation, and only surface not-yet-prompted servers:

- `_surfacedMcpAuthServers`: per-session set of server ids already prompted.
- `_setupMcpAuthPrompt`: extracted from `_observeTurn` (matching the sibling `_setupMarkdownPart` / `_setupReasoningPart` helpers). Surfaces only new servers and lists just the servers the prompt introduced, shrinking as they authenticate.
- `_reconcileSurfacedMcpAuthServers`: on `onDidChangeCustomizations`, prunes a server from the set once it reaches the running state (`McpServerStatus.Ready`). This runs independently of active turns so authentication performed while idle is still observed, and a server that later needs auth again (e.g. after a restart) re-prompts. A server that merely left `AuthRequired` for an error/stopped state stays suppressed.

### Result

Each MCP server prompts **once per conversation** if it is never authenticated, but re-prompts if it was authenticated and later needs auth again.

title: Voice: fix deferred responses not read on session switch
body:
## Summary

Fixes two bugs in the shared `VoiceSessionController` where a voice response for an unfocused session was not read out when the user switched back to that session. Both reproduce in the main window and the Agents (Sessions) window.

Expected behavior: the focused session gets live read-outs; an unfocused session that received voice input buffers its response until focused, then reads it once on focus and never again.

## Bug 1 — deferred response stranded by mismatched id spaces

The voice backend tags a **background** (unfocused) session's audio with its bare backend id (e.g. `copilotcli:/<id>`), while focus tracking, the deferred-response buffer keys, and the sessions-list pending indicator all operate in the UI **agent-host** resource space (`agent-host-<provider>:/<id>`). The two ids share the same guid but differ by scheme prefix, so a deferred response was keyed by an id that never matched the resource we flush on focus:

```
deferring response for unfocused session=copilotcli:/19b9e89e…
no buffered response matches focused=agent-host-copilotcli:/…; pending keys=[copilotcli:/19b9e89e…]
```

The response stayed buffered forever and was never read.

**Fix:** maintain a controller-owned backend→UI alias map (rebuilt from the live session list, cleared on disconnect) using the existing `toAgentHostBackendSessionUri` helper, and canonicalize each incoming `coding_session_id` once so defer/flush/pending keys share a single id space.

## Bug 2 — first on-focus narration swallowed as a "stale re-narration"

`_isStaleRenarration` blanket-dropped any unsolicited reply for a now-active idle session, including the **first-ever** narration:

```
setActiveSessionShown=copilotcli:/26ed4628 … (was <none>)
audio_response codingSessionId=copilotcli:/26ed4628 focused=copilotcli:/26ed4628 … defer=false
dropping stale re-narration for now-active idle session=copilotcli:/26ed4628   ← bug
```

The backend defers a background session's narration until it becomes active, so that reply legitimately arrives on focus and is the single on-focus read the user expects. Because nothing played, the state machine never advanced to speaking → auto-listen, leaving no mic indicator and nothing read.

**Fix:** only treat a reply as stale when a reply for that session was already heard (recorded in `_lastHeardTranscriptById`). First delivery now plays; genuine on-focus re-reads of an already-heard reply are still dropped.

## Also

- Downgraded the verbose `[voice]` diagnostic logs from `info` to `trace`.

Voice: canonicalize deferred-session ids and fix first on-focus read

The voice backend tags a background (unfocused) session's audio with its
bare backend id (e.g. copilotcli:/<id>) in the main window, while focus
tracking, the deferred-response buffer keys, and the sessions-list pending
indicator all operate in the UI agent-host resource space
(agent-host-<provider>:/<id>). A deferred response was therefore keyed by an
id that never matched the resource we flush on focus, so it stayed buffered
forever and was never read when the session became focused.

Maintain a controller-owned backend->UI alias map (rebuilt from the live
session list, cleared on disconnect) and canonicalize each incoming
coding_session_id once so defer/flush/pending keys share one id space.

Also fix _isStaleRenarration wrongly dropping the FIRST narration of a
now-active session. The backend defers a background session's narration
until it becomes active, so that reply legitimately arrives on focus and is
the single on-focus read the user expects. Only drop when a reply for the
session was already heard (recorded in _lastHeardTranscriptById). Without
this the first delivery was swallowed and the state machine never advanced
to speaking/auto-listen, leaving no mic indicator and nothing read.

Downgrade the verbose [voice] diagnostic logs from info to trace.

title: fix: forward reasoning effort on the BYOK Messages API path
body:
Taken from original PR #325119
---
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #325121 (related: #320805, #320493)

### Description

BYOK custom endpoints with `apiType: "messages"` silently drop the selected reasoning effort: the `useMessagesApi` branch of `OpenAIEndpoint.createRequestBody` returns the base body without calling `_applyReasoningEffort`, and `createMessagesRequestBody` only emits `effort` alongside a `thinking` config (adaptive or budget-based), which BYOK custom endpoints don't declare. So a custom server that declares `supportsReasoningEffort` never receives the effort selected in the picker, while the Responses and Chat Completions branches forward it correctly.

This change makes the Messages branch call `_applyReasoningEffort(body, options)` like the other two branches, and teaches `_applyReasoningEffort` a third body shape, `messages`, which writes the native Anthropic Messages field `output_config.effort` — the same shape the first-party path (`createMessagesRequestBody`) emits. That shape is the default on the Messages branch (default format: `useResponsesApi ? 'responses' : useMessagesApi ? 'messages' : 'chat-completions'`); an explicit `reasoningEffortFormat` still overrides it for servers with diverging conventions. Per the Anthropic docs, `effort` pairs with adaptive thinking on newer Claude models (`budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus/Sonnet 4.6 and rejected with a 400 on later models) and is also valid without a `thinking` config, so forwarding it is safe in every case. `_applyReasoningEffort` remains a no-op unless the model declares `supportsReasoningEffort`, scrubs any pre-populated `output_config.effort` the same way it scrubs `reasoning`/`reasoning_effort` (no double-write when the base body already carries one), and merges into `output_config` rather than replacing it so other fields (e.g. the structured-output `format`) survive.

`'messages'` is also added to the `reasoningEffortFormat` unions (`IChatModelInformation`, BYOK provider configs) and to the corresponding `package.json` configuration schema enums.

Covered by new cases in the `reasoning effort forwarding` suite of `openAIEndpoint.spec.ts`: the Messages path emits `output_config.effort` by default, a `reasoningEffortFormat: 'chat-completions'` override emits top-level `reasoning_effort` instead, and the scrub preserves sibling `output_config` fields.

### How to test

1. Configure a `customendpoint` BYOK provider with `"apiType": "messages"` against an Anthropic-Messages-compatible server, with a model declaring `"supportsReasoningEffort": ["low", "medium", "high"]` and a `reasoningEffort` set in the model settings.
2. Send a chat message and capture the outgoing request body.
3. Before: no effort field is present. After: the request carries the selected effort as the native `output_config.effort` by default, or in the shape selected by an explicit `reasoningEffortFormat` (`chat-completions` → top-level `reasoning_effort`, `responses` → nested `reasoning.effort`).
4. Unit coverage: `npx vitest run src/extension/byok/node/test/openAIEndpoint.spec.ts` from `extensions/copilot`.

Adds a project skill that turns the ["Symbolicating a crash dump" wiki section](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Native-Crash-Issues#symbolicating-a-crash-dump-steps-for-vs-code-team-members-only) into a discoverable `.github/skills/` skill.

### What it covers
- Installing `electron-minidump` and running the initial symbolication pass
- Getting and attaching the right symbol files (Insiders/Stable internal Electron vs Code-OSS Electron), including the breakpad cache hash-matching step
- **Reading the result** — identifying the crashing module (VS Code/Electron vs an injected third-party/OS DLL) and which process crashed (e.g. the extension host runs as the `node.mojom.NodeService` utility)

I tried the skill on a real report (three `.dmp` files from a user-reported extension-host crash-loop). It symbolicated cleanly and pinpointed the root cause: an `EXCEPTION_ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION` at the top of a third-party injected DLL (`ASProxy64.dll`, from Astrill VPN) inside the extension-host Node utility process — not a VS Code bug. All three dumps shared the identical signature.

Two refinements came directly out of that dry run and are included here:
- A note to **retry on transient symbol-download errors** (downloads are cached, so re-running resumes).
- A **"Reading the result"** section for attributing the crash to a module and process.

title: Add Q# language TextMate grammar
body:
This PR adds a built-in "Q# Language Basics" extension (`extensions/qsharp`) providing TextMate syntax highlighting, bracket matching, and folding for `.qs` files. Q# currently has no grammar in VS Code out of the box, any language support only exists via the [QDK extension](https://github.com/microsoft/qdk). I think this is a real gap that is worth addressing.

The grammar is vendored from the Q# Community [qsharp-community/qsharp-tmLanguage](https://github.com/qsharp-community/qsharp-tmLanguage) (MIT), following the same convention as `csharp` (I was also involved in the original [TM for C#](https://github.com/dotnet/csharp-tmLanguage), so I followed the same approach here).

It covers all syntactic aspects of modern Q# - types, `import`/`export`, `struct`/`new`, attributes, generics with class constraints, lambdas, the full operator set, all numeric literal forms and interpolated strings and so on. 

No central registration is needed - built-in grammar extensions are auto-discovered from `extensions/`.

### How to test

1. Build and run
2. Open any `.qs` file 
3. Confirm keywords, types, gates, operators, literals, and the interpolated string are highlighted. Optionally, use "Developer: Inspect Editor Tokens and Scopes" to verify scopes

The repo from which the grammar is vendored has a full suite of tests already.

title: git: honor git.detectWorktrees when opening linked worktrees
body:
### Bug
 
 Linked worktrees of an open repository are opened as separate repositories in the Source Control view **even when the user has opted out** via `git.detectWorktrees` (default `false`) and/or `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders: "never"`.
 
 They come back immediately after being closed, because they are re-discovered through several paths that never consult `git.detectWorktrees`:
 
 - `onDidChangeVisibleTextEditors` (a file open from a worktree),
 - the global `**` file-system watcher (`onPossibleGitRepositoryChange`, fires on any `/.git` change),
 - the `vscode.git` extension API `openRepository(uri)` (used by other extensions),
 
 For users with many worktrees (e.g. one per PR under review) this floods Source Control with dozens of repositories that cannot be permanently dismissed.
 
 ### Root cause
 
 `Model.isRepositoryOutsideWorkspace()` **unconditionally** treats any path that matches a worktree of an already-open repository as being *inside* the workspace:
 
 ```ts
 const worktreePaths = this.repositories.map(r => r.worktrees.map(w => w.path)).flat();
 if (worktreePaths.some(p => pathEquals(p, repositoryPath))) {
     return false;
 }
 ```
 
 Because it returns `false`, the `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders` guard in `openRepository()` never applies to worktrees, and `git.detectWorktrees` — which is supposed to control worktree discovery — is ignored on every path except the explicit `checkForWorktrees()` enumeration.
 
 ### Fix
 
 Gate that in-workspace treatment on `git.detectWorktrees`. When detection is disabled, a worktree the user did not explicitly open is treated like any other repository outside the workspace and follows `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders`.
 When detection is enabled, behavior is unchanged.
 
 ### Behavior
 
 - `git.detectWorktrees: true` → unchanged (worktrees open automatically).
 - `git.detectWorktrees: false` (default) → worktrees now obey `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders` (`never` hides them; `prompt` asks; `always` opens them), instead of always appearing.
 
 This aligns all discovery paths with the setting that already exists to control them, and makes the default (`false`) actually mean "do not auto-open worktrees".
 
 ### Verification
 
 Open a workspace whose folder is inside a repo that has linked worktrees, with `git.detectWorktrees: false` and `git.openRepositoryInParentFolders: "never"`.
 Open a file from one of the worktrees. Before: the worktree is added as a repository. After: only the workspace's repository is shown.

title: Emit restricted skillContentRead telemetry from the agent host
body:
Emits the restricted `skillContentRead` event from the agent host when a skill is loaded into a conversation, mirroring the Copilot Chat extension so the same signal is available whether chat runs in the extension or the agent host.

### What
- The agent host observes the SDK `skill.invoked` event and reports `skillContentRead` (standard GH hashed + enhanced/internal plaintext), matching the extension's `sendSkillContentReadTelemetry`.
- The SDK payload already carries everything needed — the skill content (hashed here, never sent raw), the discovery `source`, and the plugin identity — so **no SDK change is required**.
- The extension's `skillExtensionId` / `skillExtensionVersion` encode the contributing *VS Code extension*, which does not exist in the agent host; the AH-native provenance is the plugin, so `pluginName` / `pluginVersion` populate those fields.
- Fires for the main agent only, consistent with the other restricted agent-host events.

### How to test
1. Configure a skill reachable by an Agents-window session (e.g. `.github/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` in the working directory, `~/.copilot/skills/…`, or a plugin-provided skill).
2. Run a turn that invokes the skill; confirm the skill runs (synthesized skill tool-call appears).
3. A new unit test covers the reporter (`skillContentRead` emit + no-op) — `npm run test-node --grep AgentHostTelemetryReporter`.

### Known limitations & parity notes
- **Load path.** The extension emits `skillContentRead` from two paths: the skill tool *and* the read_file tool when it reads a `SKILL.md` (`isSkillMdFile`). This change covers the canonical agent-host skill-load signal (SDK `skill.invoked`) only, so a skill pulled in by directly reading its `SKILL.md` via the read tool is not captured here. A read-path hook can be added as a follow-up if the difference proves material.
- **`skill_storage` vocabulary.** The value comes straight from the SDK `source` (`project` / `inherited` / `personal-copilot` / `personal-agents` / `custom` / `plugin` / `builtin` / `remote`), which is richer than the extension's (`extension` / `internal` / `personal` / `workspace`). Same column, different value set — downstream queries should expect both.
- **`skill_path`.** Emitted as the SDK file path (vs the extension's `uri.toString()` / `file://…`); both identify the same file.
- **Scope.** Main-agent only (subagent skill loads are not reported), consistent with the other restricted agent-host events.

title: sessions: add get_session_context tool + list_sessions single-session lookup
body:
## Overview

Follow-up in the session-management tool series (after #325051 and #325139). Adds a read-only **`get_session_context`** tool so an agent can inspect an *existing* session/chat's recent conversation — e.g. to see what a session it created is doing, or to gather context before `send_message`. Also extends **`list_sessions`** with a single-session lookup so the two tools stay cleanly separated.

> **Stacked on #325139** (`send_message`) — `get_session_context` reuses that tool's link helpers. GitHub will retarget this PR's base to `main` once #325139 merges.

## `get_session_context`

Reads a compacted transcript **directly from live chat state** (`ChatState.turns` + the in-progress turn). **Deterministic only** — no plan/todo heuristics.

**Input:** `session` (a `list_sessions` URI or `agent-host-session://` link; a `create_chat` link targets that specific peer chat), `detail`, `transcriptLimit`.

**`detail` levels** (per-turn fidelity; compaction is structural, no model call, tool *outputs* never included):
- `summary` (default): per-turn `user` message + short `assistant` reply gist + `state`.
- `digest`: full assistant reply text + tool-call **names**.
- `full`: + tool-call **inputs** (truncated).

**Output:** `session`, `openLink`, `detail`, `transcript[]`, `hasMoreHistory` (from `turnsNextCursor`), `truncated`. Bounded by `transcriptLimit` (default 10, max 50). Cold/unsubscribed sessions return identity + empty transcript. Read-only, no confirmation.

## `list_sessions` single-session lookup

Adds an optional **`session`** argument: a direct lookup returning just that one session's metadata by URI / open link, **bypassing the other filters** (including the default archived exclusion).

## Clean separation
- **`list_sessions`** → session **metadata** (breadth, or one session by URI).
- **`get_session_context`** → one session's **conversation** (depth).

No overlapping surface; flow is `list_sessions` → `get_session_context` → `send_message`.

## Notes for reviewers
- `get_session_context` reads via a new `IChatContextSnapshot` accessor (`agentService._getChatContext` → `getChatState`/`getDefaultChatState`); all compaction is pure/testable in `sessionServerTools.ts`.
- Plan/todo surfacing was intentionally dropped (heuristic/unreliable); a future authoritative option would be Copilot's `rpc.plan.read()`.
- Tests: `sessionServerTools.test.ts` (25) + `serverToolGroups.test.ts` (6). `typecheck-client` + `valid-layers-check` clean.

title: Show real Mermaid error instead of "[object Object]"
body:
Fixes #325144

When a Mermaid diagram fails to render in chat, the error box showed `[object Object]` instead of the real error, hiding why the diagram didn't render.

### Cause

The Mermaid chat webview catches render failures from `mermaid.run()` and calls `createMermaidErrorElement`. Mermaid rejects those failures with a **plain object** of shape `{ str, message, hash, error }` — not an `Error` instance. The old code:

```ts
const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error);
```

fell to `String(error)` → `[object Object]`, discarding the object's usable `.message`.

### Fix

Extract the message from non-`Error` throwables (prefer `.message`, then Mermaid's `.str`) before falling back to `String(error)`. Now the box shows the actual message, e.g.:

```
Parse error on line 1:
...A -->|create_session(workspace, prompt)|
-----------------------^
Expecting 'PIPE', 'TEXT', ... got 'PS'
```

The other call site (`renderMermaidElement`, markdown preview) uses `mermaid.parse()`, which throws a real `Error`, so it was already fine and is unchanged.

### Verification

- Reproduced the `[object Object]` throwable with mermaid 11.15.0 via `mermaid.run()`.
- Confirmed the helper returns the real message for the mermaid object, real `Error`s, plain strings, empty-`message` (falls back to `str`), and `null`.
- `tsc -p preview-src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` passes; hygiene passes.

title: fix: prevent infinite loop with self-referencing handoffs in Autopilot mode (#325128)
body:
## Description

```markdown
Fixes #325128

### What was the issue

In Autopilot mode, a custom agent with `handoffs` that have `send: true` pointing to the same agent creates an infinite loop. Each response auto-triggers a handoff back to itself, which produces the same response, which triggers the handoff again — forever.

### Where was the issue

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts` — the `renderChatSuggestNextWidget()` method. When Autopilot is active and a response carries handoffs with `send: true`, the code auto-triggers the first matching handoff via `handleNextPromptSelection()` without checking whether the handoff targets the same mode that produced the response. The Copilot ToolCallingLoop correctly stops when the model produces a text-only response, but the handoff auto-trigger in the UI layer creates a new turn that restarts the cycle.

### How it was fixed

A single guard added at line 1351 in `renderChatSuggestNextWidget()`:

```diff
- if (autoSendHandoff) {
+ if (autoSendHandoff && autoSendHandoff.agent !== responseMode.name.get()) {
```

Before auto-triggering a `send: true` handoff, the code now compares the handoff's target agent against the name of the mode that produced the response. If they match (self-referencing), the auto-trigger is skipped. Handoff buttons are still rendered for manual use — only the automatic send is blocked for self-referencing handoffs.

### Why this method over others

- **Guard in the ToolCallingLoop**: not viable — the loop has no visibility into handoffs, which live in the chat widget UI layer above it.
- **Depth counter / cycle detector**: over-engineered for a single equality check, adds state and complexity.
- **Guard at the auto-trigger point (chosen)**: the fix lives exactly where the loop forms — minimal (1 condition), stateless, uses existing types (`IHandOff.agent`, `IChatMode.name`) already in scope. No new imports, no behavior change for legitimate cross-agent handoffs.

### How to test

1. Create a `.agent.md` file with a self-referencing handoff:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: test agent
   description: 'A custom agent with handoffs.'
   tools: [vscode, execute, read, agent, edit, search, web, browser, todo]
   handoffs:
     - label: Button 1
       agent: 'test agent'
       prompt: This is a handoff from Button 1.
       send: true
     - label: Button 2
       agent: 'test agent'
       prompt: This is a handoff from Button 2.
       send: true
   ---
   Always reply with 'Hi, I'm your custom agent. How can I assist you today?'
   ```

2. Enable Autopilot mode and select the "test agent" mode
3. Send "Hi"
   - **Before**: infinite loop of auto-triggered handoffs
   - **After**: one response rendered, handoff buttons displayed, no auto-trigger
4. Verify handoff buttons are visible and clickable for manual use
5. Verify a Plan → Agent handoff with `send: true` still auto-triggers (different agents should work normally)

body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #325051 (the session-management tool suite). Adds two host-owned server tools so an agent can **act on** and **observe** existing Agent Host sessions/chats.

## Tools

### `send_message`
Starts a new turn on an *existing* session or chat (e.g. one just created with `create_session`/`create_chat`), reusing the same `startPrompt` delivery path. Fire-and-forget (no reply awaited), requires confirmation, guarded by a self-loop check (refuses the exact chat channel it runs on) and a process-wide fan-out cap. Renders the deterministic "Open Session" pill (conversation icon when chat-scoped). Accepts a `list_sessions` URI or `agent-host-session://` link; a `create_chat` link targets that specific peer chat.

### `get_session_context`
Read-only. Returns a compacted **transcript** of a session/chat's recent turns, read directly from live chat state — **deterministic only**, no plan/todo heuristics. Three fidelity levels via `detail`:
- `summary` (default): per-turn message + short reply gist + state.
- `digest`: + full assistant reply text + tool-call names.
- `full`: + tool-call inputs (truncated).

Bounded by `transcriptLimit` (default 10, max 50) with `hasMoreHistory`/`truncated` flags; includes the in-progress turn. Cold sessions return identity + empty transcript.

### `list_sessions` — single-session lookup
Adds an optional `session` argument: a direct lookup returning one session's metadata by URI / open link, bypassing the other filters (incl. the default archived exclusion).

## Clean separation
- `list_sessions` → session **metadata** (breadth, or one session by URI).
- `get_session_context` → one session's **conversation** (depth).

Flow: `list_sessions` → `get_session_context` → `send_message`.

## Notes for reviewers
- Both tools follow the existing server-tool pattern; `get_session_context` reads via a new `IChatContextSnapshot` accessor (`getChatState`/`getDefaultChatState`), all compaction pure/testable in `sessionServerTools.ts`.

title: Voice: keep hands-free listening when switching sessions without dictation
body:
### Bug

In voice hands-free mode, if the mic was idly listening (nothing dictated yet) and the user clicked **New Chat** (or otherwise switched the visible session), the listening indicator was immediately dropped.

### Root cause

The chat view's transcript autorun (`chatViewPane.ts`) called `stopListening()` whenever `_currentSessionResource` changed while `voiceState === 'listening'`. This guard exists to avoid misrouting an **in-progress dictation** to the newly focused session, but it fired unconditionally — even when nothing had been recorded yet — so switching sessions killed an otherwise-idle listening turn.

### Fix

Only stop listening when there is actual in-progress dictation (a partial user turn with non-empty text). Otherwise keep listening and re-anchor `listeningSession`/`ownerSession` to the newly focused session so hands-free listening follows the user into the new chat.

### Testing

Verified against the running dev build: run a voice command in a session → wait for listening → click New Chat → listening now persists instead of dropping to idle.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

title: sessions: align add-tab keybindings with workbench view shortcuts
body:
## What

Aligns the Agents window add-tab (`+`) actions with the keybindings of their equivalent workbench views, and shows those keybindings in the `+` dropdown menu.

| Tab | Keybinding | Matches workbench view |
|------|------------|------------------------|
| Files (empty file editor) | `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+E` | Explorer |
| Search | `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+F` | Search |
| Changes | `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+G` (mac `Ctrl+Shift+G`) | Source Control |
| Browser | `Cmd+Shift+B` | (no workbench equivalent) |

## Why

- The **Browser** action previously used the chord `Cmd+Shift+K B`. Because it starts with `Cmd+Shift+K`, it swallowed the **Delete Line** shortcut in the Agents window (VS Code waited for the second chord key). It now uses a single `Cmd+Shift+B` binding.
- The other add-tab actions used ad-hoc chords (`Cmd+K B` for Files, `Cmd+K S` for Search) that were inconsistent with the rest of the workbench. They now mirror the corresponding view shortcuts so the bindings are predictable.
- The **Changes** action previously had no keybinding; it now reuses the Source Control binding.

## Notes for reviewers

- All bindings are scoped to the Agents window via `addTabActionWhen` (`IsSessionsWindowContext && !IsAuxiliaryWindowContext`), so they don't collide in the normal editor window.
- The `+` dropdown now passes a `keybindingProvider` so each menu item renders its shortcut.
- Removed the now-unused `KeyChord` import from `addTabActions.ts`.
- Also includes a minor style fix in `sessionChangesEditor.css` (drops a redundant `font-weight: semiBold`).

Also makes the bar collapse its labelled buttons to **icon-only** when the tabs title gets narrow.

In the single-pane layout the Create Pull Request action fits more naturally alongside the docked Changes editor's tab bar than in the session title bar, and it needs to yield horizontal room to the tabs when space is tight.

The observer retries across a few animation frames while the toolbar attaches and falls back to `.editor-group-container` when there is no `.tabs-and-actions-container`.

title: Forward reasoning effort on the BYOK custom endpoint Messages API path
body:

* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #325121 (related: #320805, #320493)

### Description

BYOK custom endpoints with `apiType: "messages"` silently drop the selected reasoning effort: the `useMessagesApi` branch of `OpenAIEndpoint.createRequestBody` returns the base body without calling `_applyReasoningEffort`, and `createMessagesRequestBody` only emits `effort` alongside a `thinking` config (adaptive or budget-based), which BYOK custom endpoints don't declare. So a custom server that declares `supportsReasoningEffort` never receives the effort selected in the picker, while the Responses and Chat Completions branches forward it correctly.

This change makes the Messages branch call `_applyReasoningEffort(body, options)` like the other two branches, and teaches `_applyReasoningEffort` a third body shape, `messages`, which writes the native Anthropic Messages field `output_config.effort` — the same shape the first-party path (`createMessagesRequestBody`) emits. That shape is the default on the Messages branch (default format: `useResponsesApi ? 'responses' : useMessagesApi ? 'messages' : 'chat-completions'`); an explicit `reasoningEffortFormat` still overrides it for servers with diverging conventions. Per the Anthropic docs, `effort` pairs with adaptive thinking on newer Claude models (`budget_tokens` is deprecated on Opus/Sonnet 4.6 and rejected with a 400 on later models) and is also valid without a `thinking` config, so forwarding it is safe in every case. `_applyReasoningEffort` remains a no-op unless the model declares `supportsReasoningEffort`, scrubs any pre-populated `output_config.effort` the same way it scrubs `reasoning`/`reasoning_effort` (no double-write when the base body already carries one), and merges into `output_config` rather than replacing it so other fields (e.g. the structured-output `format`) survive.

`'messages'` is also added to the `reasoningEffortFormat` unions (`IChatModelInformation`, BYOK provider configs) and to the corresponding `package.json` configuration schema enums.

Covered by new cases in the `reasoning effort forwarding` suite of `openAIEndpoint.spec.ts`: the Messages path emits `output_config.effort` by default, a `reasoningEffortFormat: 'chat-completions'` override emits top-level `reasoning_effort` instead, and the scrub preserves sibling `output_config` fields.

### How to test

1. Configure a `customendpoint` BYOK provider with `"apiType": "messages"` against an Anthropic-Messages-compatible server, with a model declaring `"supportsReasoningEffort": ["low", "medium", "high"]` and a `reasoningEffort` set in the model settings.
2. Send a chat message and capture the outgoing request body.
3. Before: no effort field is present. After: the request carries the selected effort as the native `output_config.effort` by default, or in the shape selected by an explicit `reasoningEffortFormat` (`chat-completions` → top-level `reasoning_effort`, `responses` → nested `reasoning.effort`).
4. Unit coverage: `npx vitest run src/extension/byok/node/test/openAIEndpoint.spec.ts` from `extensions/copilot`.
